create.name: Michael Ventura
create.bio:
Michael Ventura is an author and teacher whose work centres on empathy and purpose, and on the older healing ways that sit underneath them. For close to twenty years he ran Sub Rosa, a strategy and design studio in New York, where he developed methods for putting empathy to practical use with organisations such as the ACLU, Google and the United Nations. That work became his 2018 book Applied Empathy, and his second book, Constellation Thinking, due in January 2027, treats purpose as a set of related pursuits rather than one fixed goal. He has taught as visiting faculty at Princeton, West Point and Michigan's Ross School of Business.

Alongside this he has kept a private practice for more than a decade under the name Corvus Medicine. He trained in qigong with Master Yuwen Ru and in the curanderismo of the Nahua peoples of Mexico with the curandera Doña Leova, and his sessions pair qigong with the limpia, a ritual cleansing, sometimes adding plants, sound and crystals. As an ordained minister he also holds ceremonies for births, marriages, homes and the dying. At Esalen in Big Sur he leads weekend workshops on these folk traditions with Margaret Harrsen. He is board president of the Tribal Link Foundation, which supports Indigenous leaders, and writes a Substack on empathy and meaning.

books.title: Applied Empathy: The New Language of Leadership
books.author: Michael Ventura
books.description: His first book, published by Touchstone in 2018, which argues that empathy is a skill people can learn and use at work rather than a fixed trait. It sets out the approach he built with clients and students over his years running a design studio.

books.title: Constellation Thinking: Create a Life of Purpose Without a North Star
books.author: Michael Ventura
books.description: A book due from Authors Equity in January 2027 that questions the idea of a single life purpose. Readers map several pursuits that matter to them and look at how they relate, drawing on systems thinking and contemplative practice.

courses.title: Natural Healing: A Spiritual Journey of Return
courses.description: A weekend at Esalen in Big Sur, co-led with Margaret Harrsen, introducing curanderismo, the folk tradition of Mexico. The days mix morning movement and meditation with egg and herb cleansings, abdominal work, evening flower baths and exercises in listening to one another.

courses.title: Corvus Medicine Sessions
courses.description: One-to-one sessions that combine qigong with a limpia, the cleansing ritual of the Nahua tradition, to work on body, mind and spirit together. Appointments are arranged through his Corvus Medicine website.

courses.title: Corvus Medicine Ceremonies
courses.description: Ceremonies drawn from ancestral practice for life passages: welcoming a newborn, marriage (he is an ordained minister), clearing a home, and accompanying people at the end of life and their families.
